title: The Baker’s Wife at Classic Stage Company #thebakerswife #arianadebos...
transcript: The Baker's Wife is a very strange musical and I can see why it's seldom produced. Classic Stage Company's current production features an all-star cast and some charming direction, but that can only go so far. In a small provincial town in France where everyone knows everyone's business, the community is in dire need of a new baker. The Castagnets arrive and immediately become the talk of the town. The Baker's wife, played by Oscar winner Ariana DeBose, is greatly aware of the speculation surrounding her marriage to a much older man, and feeling restless, makes a decision that turns the community upside down and jeopardizes their bread. If this description makes the stakes feel low, it's because they are. But the script is funny and the performances here are wonderful — every community member is drawn with specificity and charm, and the score by Stephen Schwartz is lovely, despite every song being a little too long. But perhaps that's a good way to fill up the two acts, as not a lot actually happens. And I gotta say, the role of the Baker's Wife is pretty modest, considering it's the title character. I wish more attention was given to her and her emotional journey than some of the less relevant characters. Overall, a solid production of a musical that's not really my cup of tea — but if nothing else, it was worth seeing for this cast. With that, another program for my collection.
